title: Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 1)
plain_meaning: The electrical circuit controlling variable valve timing on bank 1 has a fault.
common_causes: Faulty camshaft actuator solenoid; wiring or connector damage; low or dirty engine oil

title: Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 1)
plain_meaning: Valve timing is more advanced than the engine computer expected.
common_causes: Dirty or low engine oil; stuck oil control valve; worn timing chain

title: Crankshaft/Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A)
plain_meaning: The crankshaft and camshaft are out of step with each other.
common_causes: Stretched or jumped timing chain; failed cam or crank sensor; oil control valve stuck

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain_meaning: The heater inside the front oxygen sensor is not working.
common_causes: Failed oxygen sensor heater; blown fuse; broken wiring

title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
plain_meaning: The outside air temperature reading looks wrong.
common_causes: Failed ambient temperature sensor; wiring fault; sensor blocked by debris

title: Fuel Rail/System Pressure Too Low
plain_meaning: Fuel pressure is below what the engine needs.
common_causes: Clogged fuel filter; weak fuel pump; leaking pressure regulator; restricted fuel line

title: Mass Air Flow Circuit Range/Performance
plain_meaning: The air flow sensor reading does not match what the engine is actually doing.
common_causes: Dirty MAF sensor; air filter clogged; vacuum leak; leaking intake boot

title: Mass Air Flow Circuit Low Input
plain_meaning: The air flow sensor is reporting less air than is possible.
common_causes: Disconnected or dirty MAF sensor; wiring short; severely blocked air filter

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit High Input
plain_meaning: The intake air temperature sensor is reading abnormally high.
common_causes: Failed IAT sensor; open circuit in wiring; corroded connector

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Circuit Low Input
plain_meaning: The coolant temperature sensor is reading abnormally low.
common_causes: Failed coolant temperature sensor; short in wiring; bad connector

title: Throttle Position Sensor Range/Performance
plain_meaning: The throttle position reading does not match engine behaviour.
common_causes: Dirty throttle body; failing throttle position sensor; damaged wiring

title: Coolant Thermostat Below Regulating Temperature
plain_meaning: The engine is not warming up as fast as it should.
common_causes: Thermostat stuck open; failed coolant temperature sensor; low coolant level

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain_meaning: The front oxygen sensor voltage is stuck low.
common_causes: Failed oxygen sensor; exhaust leak before the sensor; wiring fault

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain_meaning: The front oxygen sensor is reacting too slowly.
common_causes: Aged oxygen sensor; contamination from oil or coolant burning; exhaust leak

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain_meaning: The heater in the front oxygen sensor has failed.
common_causes: Failed sensor heater element; blown fuse; damaged wiring harness

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
plain_meaning: The rear oxygen sensor signal is faulty.
common_causes: Failed rear oxygen sensor; exhaust leak near sensor; corroded connector

title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
plain_meaning: The engine is getting too much air or not enough fuel.
common_causes: Vacuum leak; dirty MAF sensor; weak fuel pump; clogged fuel filter; leaking intake gasket

title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
plain_meaning: The engine is getting too much fuel or not enough air.
common_causes: Leaking fuel injector; failed fuel pressure regulator; dirty air filter; faulty oxygen sensor

title: System Too Lean (Bank 2)
plain_meaning: Bank 2 of the engine is getting too much air or not enough fuel.
common_causes: Vacuum leak on bank 2; dirty MAF sensor; weak fuel delivery

title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
plain_meaning: More than one cylinder is misfiring and the computer cannot tell which.
common_causes: Worn spark plugs; failing ignition coils; vacuum leak; low fuel pressure; low compression

title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
plain_meaning: Cylinder 1 is not burning fuel properly.
common_causes: Worn spark plug; failed ignition coil; clogged injector; low compression in that cylinder

title: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected
plain_meaning: Cylinder 2 is not burning fuel properly.
common_causes: Worn spark plug; failed ignition coil; clogged injector; low compression in that cylinder

title: Cylinder 3 Misfire Detected
plain_meaning: Cylinder 3 is not burning fuel properly.
common_causes: Worn spark plug; failed ignition coil; clogged injector; low compression in that cylinder

title: Cylinder 4 Misfire Detected
plain_meaning: Cylinder 4 is not burning fuel properly.
common_causes: Worn spark plug; failed ignition coil; clogged injector; low compression in that cylinder

title: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit (Bank 1)
plain_meaning: The sensor that listens for engine knock has a circuit fault.
common_causes: Failed knock sensor; damaged wiring; loose sensor mounting

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit
plain_meaning: The sensor that tracks crankshaft rotation is faulty.
common_causes: Failed crankshaft position sensor; damaged reluctor ring; wiring fault

title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit (Bank 1)
plain_meaning: The sensor that tracks camshaft position is faulty.
common_causes: Failed camshaft position sensor; wiring or connector damage; timing chain issue

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Insufficient
plain_meaning: Not enough exhaust gas is being recirculated back into the engine.
common_causes: Clogged EGR passages; stuck EGR valve; failed EGR position sensor; carbon buildup

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Excessive
plain_meaning: Too much exhaust gas is being recirculated.
common_causes: EGR valve stuck open; failed EGR solenoid; carbon holding the valve open

title: Secondary Air Injection System Incorrect Flow
plain_meaning: The secondary air pump system is not flowing correctly.
common_causes: Failed air pump; blocked air passages; stuck check valve

title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
plain_meaning: The catalytic converter is not cleaning the exhaust as well as it should.
common_causes: Worn catalytic converter; failed rear oxygen sensor; exhaust leak; engine running rich or lean for a long time

title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
plain_meaning: The bank 2 catalytic converter is not cleaning the exhaust well enough.
common_causes: Worn catalytic converter; failed rear oxygen sensor; exhaust leak

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Malfunction
plain_meaning: The fuel vapour system has a general fault.
common_causes: Loose or faulty fuel cap; cracked vapour hose; failed purge valve

title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Small Leak)
plain_meaning: A small leak was found in the fuel vapour system.
common_causes: Loose fuel cap; small crack in a vapour hose; failed purge or vent valve

title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Large Leak)
plain_meaning: A large leak was found in the fuel vapour system.
common_causes: Missing or badly sealed fuel cap; disconnected vapour hose; failed vent valve

title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Very Small Leak)
plain_meaning: A very small leak was found in the fuel vapour system.
common_causes: Fuel cap seal worn; hairline crack in vapour line; sticking vent valve

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A
plain_meaning: The vehicle speed signal is missing or wrong.
common_causes: Failed speed sensor; damaged wiring; faulty ABS module

title: Idle Air Control System
plain_meaning: The engine cannot hold a steady idle.
common_causes: Dirty throttle body; failed idle air control valve; vacuum leak

title: Idle Air Control System RPM Lower Than Expected
plain_meaning: The engine idles slower than it should.
common_causes: Carbon buildup in throttle body; sticking IAC valve; vacuum restriction

title: Idle Air Control System RPM Higher Than Expected
plain_meaning: The engine idles faster than it should.
common_causes: Vacuum leak; stuck throttle plate; failed IAC valve

title: System Voltage Low
plain_meaning: The electrical system voltage is below normal.
common_causes: Failing alternator; worn battery; loose or corroded battery terminals; bad ground

title: System Voltage High
plain_meaning: The electrical system voltage is above normal.
common_causes: Faulty voltage regulator; failing alternator; bad battery connection

title: PCM Processor Fault
plain_meaning: The engine control module itself has an internal fault.
common_causes: Failed engine control module; power or ground fault to the module; water ingress

title: Transmission Control System Malfunction
plain_meaning: The transmission control system has logged a fault.
common_causes: Transmission fault stored separately; low transmission fluid; failed solenoid; wiring fault

title: Incorrect Gear Ratio
plain_meaning: The gear engaged does not match the gear commanded.
common_causes: Low or burnt transmission fluid; worn clutch packs; failed shift solenoid

title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Performance
plain_meaning: The torque converter lock-up clutch is slipping or not engaging.
common_causes: Failed torque converter clutch solenoid; low transmission fluid; worn converter

title: Shift Solenoid B Malfunction
plain_meaning: A transmission shift solenoid is not working.
common_causes: Failed shift solenoid; dirty transmission fluid; wiring fault

title: Driver Frontal Stage 1 Deployment Control
plain_meaning: A fault in the driver airbag deployment circuit.
common_causes: Failed airbag clock spring; damaged wiring under seat; faulty airbag module

title: Driver Seat Position Sensor
plain_meaning: The driver seat position sensor is faulty.
common_causes: Failed position sensor; damaged wiring under the seat

title: Battery Voltage Low
plain_meaning: The body control module sees low battery voltage.
common_causes: Weak battery; failing alternator; corroded terminals

title: Left Front Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit
plain_meaning: The left front wheel speed sensor signal is faulty.
common_causes: Failed wheel speed sensor; damaged wiring at the wheel; dirty tone ring

title: Right Front Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit
plain_meaning: The right front wheel speed sensor signal is faulty.
common_causes: Failed wheel speed sensor; damaged wiring at the wheel; dirty tone ring

title: Left Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit
plain_meaning: The left rear wheel speed sensor signal is faulty.
common_causes: Failed wheel speed sensor; harness damage; corroded connector

title: Steering Wheel Position Sensor
plain_meaning: The steering angle sensor is reporting a fault.
common_causes: Sensor needs recalibration after alignment; failed sensor; clock spring fault

title: ABS Pump Motor Circuit
plain_meaning: The ABS pump motor circuit has a fault.
common_causes: Failed ABS pump motor; blown fuse; failed ABS module

title: Valve Relay Circuit
plain_meaning: The ABS valve relay circuit is faulty.
common_causes: Failed relay; ABS module fault; wiring damage

title: EBCM Relay Circuit
plain_meaning: The electronic brake control module relay has a fault.
common_causes: Failed relay; corroded connector; failed brake control module

title: Lost Communication With ECM/PCM A
plain_meaning: Modules cannot talk to the engine control module.
common_causes: Failed engine control module; broken CAN bus wiring; poor ground; low battery voltage

title: Lost Communication With ABS Control Module
plain_meaning: Modules cannot talk to the ABS control module.
common_causes: Failed ABS module; CAN bus wiring fault; blown fuse

title: Lost Communication With Body Control Module
plain_meaning: Modules cannot talk to the body control module.
common_causes: Failed body control module; CAN wiring damage; water ingress in a connector

title: Lost Communication With Instrument Panel Cluster
plain_meaning: Modules cannot talk to the dashboard cluster.
common_causes: Failed instrument cluster; CAN bus fault; blown fuse

title: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Lean (Bank 1)
plain_meaning: Fuel trim after the catalytic converter is running lean.
common_causes: Exhaust leak after the converter; failed rear oxygen sensor; worn converter

title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
plain_meaning: The rear oxygen sensor signal is stuck on the lean side.
common_causes: Failed rear oxygen sensor; exhaust leak; wiring fault
